beats.summary: Clark uses a Star Trek reference to end his interview with Dwight, claiming he 'Kobayashi Maru'd' the process and gets the job.

evidence.snippet: Clark: So I'd Kobayashi Maru it.
Clark: This interview's over, and I get the job. I just Kobayashi Maru'd the whole process.

beats.summary: Dwight interviews his cousin Mose for a sales position, questioning the accuracy of Mose's resume.

evidence.snippet:
Dwight: What quality would make you a good sales associate?
Mose: People person.

Dwight: You know we live together, right?
Mose: Yes.
Dwight: And I've never seen you go to work, ever.

beats.summary: Several candidates for the sales position reveal their connections to Dwight, including family and past relationships.

evidence.snippet:
Clark: So you guys all know Dwight already?
Melvina: I was his babysitter, and then we dated for a while.
Zeke: Dwight's my cousin, so I overheard him telling my brother Mose about the job opportunity in the shower.

beats.summary: Dwight reveals he attended a fake private school that claimed to teach mutant abilities, which was a con.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: When I was young, I spent several years at a private school where I was told I would be taught to harness my mutant abilities.

beats.summary: Jim expresses frustration about Dwight hiring unusual people and discusses with David Wallace the implications of his part-time work and pay.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Okay, here's one. A customer who ordered enough paper to qualify for a volume discount now wants to return half the stock. You can't rebate the sales price or credit for future purchases because you brokered the deal for a third par

beats.summary: Dwight compares his friends to Spider-man, while others mock the weirdness of his hires.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: You know who else was a freak? Spider-man. And he was also a hero.
Darryl: Your friends are like Spider-man, if he had gotten bitten by a spider and then got really into masturbating.
